analysis.title: Global Reflections - 23 Oct 2026
key_insights: GS sees the AI complex in a hedge fund deleveraging episode. The AI vs AI At Risk Pair (GSPUARTI) is down double digits YTD and the S&P ex AI (SPXXAI) has overtaken the S&P 500 on YTD returns.
90% of GS Prime book GMV is quants and multi-managers, so short-term stops matter more than medium-term value in this deleveraging.
GS work on the momentum factor and AI valuations supports buying the dip and repositioning selectively into AI, starting with Power, Hyperscalers, Inference and Cyber.

Cyclical headwinds of slowing growth, higher oil prices, tighter financial conditions and a tightening cycle remain. GS would use GSXUCYCL as a funding short alongside Low Quality expressions (NPTC, LOWQ, DEBT).
Beta adjusted nets fell 3.5 pts on the week and 10.3 pts on the month. They are at a 1-year low, the 14th percentile on a 3-year look back and the 33rd percentile on a 5-year look back.
META results and Prime Book color show the market is focused on AI financing, return on capital and positioning. HFs de-grossed in 7 of the last 8 sessions at an accelerating pace.
Infotech saw long selling and short additions. Net allocation to Semis and Semicap Equipment is at its lowest level this year.

GS says scepticism and uncertainty should not be confused with overvaluation. It prefers Power (GSX1POW1) as midterm concerns fade, and datacentre equipment (GSTMTDAT) as the beneficiary of hyperscaler capex, where earnings show no sign of slowing while prices have faded since summer.

Healthcare is an AI-uncorrelated pocket benefitting from using AI (GSHLCAIP, recently rebalanced). Beneficiaries fall into four groups: AI diagnostics and precision medicine, AI infrastructure and picks-and-shovels, AI drug discovery and clinical development, and operational productivity.
The High Beta Momentum Pair (GSPRHIMO) has erased all YTD gains after a 43% drawdown from its ~70% June peak. It is re-testing July lows.
AI Beneficiaries (GSTMTAIP) had their worst day versus SPXXAI since DeepSeek Monday. SPXXAI has closed the gap with SPX (+6.5% in Oct).

GS sees buying the dip in momentum as better risk/reward. Positioning is cleaner (lowest since June 2025, still 73rd percentile), drawdown is elevated versus history and earnings of the winners have risen steadily.

UK Consumer Confidence had its largest ex-Covid decline since Brexit on cost of living concerns. The UK Consumer basket (GSXEUKCO) is up 10% over the last month on a momentum unwind, at 13x PE, above the 90th percentile of its 3-year history.
GS expects possible tax increases at next week's Autumn Budget, a widely expected BoE hike in November and weak 3Q reporting to reverse the recent squeeze in GSXEUKCO.

On China, stronger-than-expected economic data has not offset concerns about domestic demand and the AI unwind. Friday's rebound came from buying in national-team-linked ETFs, which suggests policy support is active, but investors still will not deploy risk meaningfully.
GS continues to see demand for high dividend defensives (GSXACHHN) over AI growth (GSXACART) in China.
Hyperscalers (GSXUHYPR) earnings expectations have not been revised since July.

GS rebalanced the Power Up America basket (GSENEPOW) toward behind-the-meter forecasts. It cut utilities weight while keeping leading IPPs higher, excluded exploration and production, and raised alternatives and behind-the-meter/on-campus generation. GS expects the group to benefit from infrastructure spending beyond the hyperscaler capex cycle.

Policy support is active but investors are waiting for a durable catalyst. GS prefers high dividend defensives over AI growth.
